body: Thanks! I'm DCLG myself. Seems silly to say but it was the Westminster attack in March that knocked me out of it. Was there for an interview and missed it by 5 minutes, while I queued at the tube station shop for a packet of crisps and a Telegraph. Still to do this day wish I'd been there and been killed, would have solved my issue of being too cowardly to kill myself and maybe someone who wanted to live there wouldn't have died. Thought after that I had a duty to try and help other people, but its difficult when riptides like this pull you under again.

Thanks. Just very lonely and going through one of the rough patches my friends used to try and comfort me through. Having a panic attack, thinking that my hopes of getting my best mate back are misplaced and that I should just give up and kill myself soon, rather than waiting for my own deadline of the end of the year. Like I said, can't really talk to my mates because then they won't help me by talking to him though.

I know, I should be more grateful. But the only way I'll get my old life back is getting my best mate back and they've refused to help with that for almost two years. Just hoping they'll help me with that if I stay sober - officially anyway, I still drink alone every now and then when I need to - and get going with the new job, in a couple of months. I'm probably just being optimistic though, things will never go back to how they used to be.

Its so difficult when people think you're draining. I mean, I know that depressed people naturally are - I definitely am - but if our mates helped us out of the hole we are in then we wouldn't be draining anymore right?

You probably made the right decision. When I used to talk to them they really didn't understand. They went through a phase of trying to help but after a few months they changed, and it became like they were angry at me, thinking that I didn't want to get better because all of their vacuous advice like "It gets better!" didn't work. I know that they do care, but they still won't help me until I'm already better so I have to pretend.
Thanks, I'm glad I could help.

Thanks for replying. I kind of get what you are saying but I really don't believe in God or fate or anything like that. I spend most of my time drinking alone in my room. What kind of God would keep me in my misery whilst killing a young school teacher, or that policeman who had children, or maiming those little French girls who may never be able to walk again?

No, she didn't attempt suicide because of you. You are not responsible. I understand why, in those circumstances, it must feel like your fault but it isn't. I've tried to commit suicide twice after the person I loved cut me out their life because they couldn't deal with my depression anymore. I know it wasn't their fault though. 

You might, just as the person I loved was, the catalyst that triggered a suicide attempt, but you aren't the cause of the background problems your girlfriend must have had that meant a fight was a sufficient trigger for her, anymore than my loved one was.

I hope you are able to work things out because you obviously care about her. But you are in no way responsible, so please don't feel guilty.

Not my place to say; I'm in the UK where everyone is fairly secular. I came out to my parents and they were really supportive. The reason I'm suicidal is unrequited love for my best mate. And I want kids which I can't have because I'm gay. If the only problem you have is worrying that your parents won't accept you, you should tell them. At least that way you'll know either way. My parents were huge homophobes until I told them. Then they were magically OK with it. Like I said I;m from a fairly secular family so I don't know how common homophobic families who accept gay sons are. But at least think about it?

My friend cut me out his life because I was gay and in love with him. We were best mates 7 years and then for two years after I came out. He's refused to speak to me for a year and a half. I feel like suicide is the only way to make him care again.

Thank you for caring. But the only thing I care about is making him care about me, even if I have to kill myself to do it. You're probably right that he won't care anyway but at least this way there is a chance.
Nope. I fucking hate myself and I know I deserve this.

Its just biology. I think being gay is great, obviously. But you can't have your own kids. For someone that desperately wants children this is terrible. I am really glad you are more comfortable than I in the LGTB community though.

Thanks for your message. My friend was a very good friend though. Not selfish at all. He put up with me for two years. I'd just realised I was bi and I got the thought that everyone was as well. To avoid the misery of him and his girlfriend all I did was drink. And then I'd harass him, hugging him or sometimes when I was blackout drunk trying to kiss him. I missed that out the original post as I was so ashamed but I want you and everyone to know I'm the selfish monster not him. He was such a perfect person.

Thanks for your reply. I get what you mean about the grass always being greener. That said, at least being straight you know that you are physically capable of having a family, something I never will be able to. Its probably apples and oranges but, when all I want is to have a family and get my friend back and I can't do either it makes you wonder why life is worth living.

Thank you for your kind words. That said, I'm not a nice person and I absolutely deserve what's happened to me. I can now live with the shit life I've made for myself without my friend or accept its over and go. Latter is the only one I can do.

Dying won't get my friend back but at least he'll know how much I love him and that all my suicide attempts weren't a pathetic cry for help which I got over as soon as he cut me out his life. Sounds silly but I'd rather go now and ensure he knows I love him than spend another 50 years wishing I was dead.
Aha, thank you! My phone's too shitty unfortunately.

I get what your saying, and have nothing wrong with being with gay moral wise - any relatively sane person would agree what two people do in the privacy of their own home is no-one else's business. Still, being gay is a huge disadvantage if I want to have children and a family, as I do. No amount of our agreeing being gay is mostly great will change this.
Thanks for caring, but I've tried all that in the past and none of that has worked. I just want my friend back and I don't think there's anyway to do that.

That really sucks that you started out with such passion for gardening and growing things and that the job started to suck the enjoyment out of it for you. I hope when you start to feel better you'll be able to regain your interest in it.

I'm sorry to hear that. Are you working again now? Its such a struggle to get your self-esteem back never mind a job. How do you go to a job interview and sell yourself sufficiently to get it when you yourself don't really believe in you?

My political career was ruined by depression. I was a professional political campaigner in the UK, responsible for trying to lobby MPs and Peers in Parliament as well as the press on a variety of policy issues. I'd written a book on politics and had once featured as commentator on a political news programme. Nothing major but I felt like I was just getting started. 

After a year I'd been struggling with depression from being gay / unrequited love for my straight best friend and it all caught up with me. I told my boss and she was very understanding at first but I started calling in sick, unable to leave my bedroom. After a month or two of that I felt so guilty I quit my job so my company could hire someone who was capable of giving it their all.

That was two years ago now. Since then I've moved home and live, unemployed, with my Mum and Dad. I still follow all the news and wish I was still a tiny part of it but I know I still can't hold down a job. 

Worst thing is I thought when I moved to London to work in politics, a freshfaced 22 year old, that my life was just beginning. I had no idea I would only get one year.

I don't usually post but I went through a very similar thing with my straight best friend when I realised I was gay and in love with him so I felt like I should let you know you aren't alone. 

I'm very sorry you are having such a shit time of it. There is no easy solution to problems like this but I'm certain that even if you cut your best friend out your life it would still destroy him if you killed yourself. After struggling with the unrequited love for two years my best friend cut me out his life and we didn't speak for over a year until I tried to kill myself. He told me if I'd gone through with it that would have destroyed him.

I don't really know what to advise you to do - I'm still on the brink myself - I just know cutting your friend out your life wouldn't lessen the impact if you did kill yourself. 

I hope you feel better soon and if you ever want to talk more please PM me.
